title: French local-use missal book states: Paris, Rouen, Langres, Uzès and selected diocesan prints

sources.title: Usuarium book 7371, Missale Parisiense, BnF B-178

sources.title: Anthony Ward, Euchology for the Mass In Cena Domini, Notitiae 44 (2008), 611–634
sources.inspection: Read printed pp. 633–634, PDF pp. 59–60, including Ward’s citation of 1738MP no. 1060 as the Maundy Thursday postcommunion and his source discussion. This is a modern scholarly description, not original 1738-image collation.
sources.limitations: Ward’s description alone cannot date first introduction to 1738; the earlier Paris missal annotation requires direct examination of 1685 and 1705.

sources.title: Gerard O’Connor, annotated orations of the 1738 Missale Parisiense
sources.inspection: Read prayer index entry 1060 and the MP abbreviation as already recorded in the Western inventory; MP refers to Paris missals of 1685 and 1705 collectively. The web text is an edited concordance, not an original printing.
sources.limitations: The aggregate MP notation does not by itself prove the exact wording in both 1685 and 1705 copies or the first edition carrying the prayer.

sources.title: Usuarium book 7090, Missale ecclesiae Rotomagensis, BM Lyon 20390
sources.inspection: Read the edition-identified Usuarium entry: Rouen, original title Missale ecclesiae Rotomagensis, catalogue age 1728, BM Lyon 20390, Amiet 1364; compared the Amiet 1364 catalogue row also listing Usuarium 7461.
sources.limitations: No original book pages, printer, prayers, approval or use record inspected. Usuarium 7461 is a possible duplicate bibliographic representation, not an independently established textual version.

stages.label: 1481 Paris Missale Parisiense
stages.scope: Identified book witness and the Eucharistic components supported by the cited original leaves or edition-identified contents index; no complete reconstructed missal.
stages.summary: The 1481 Paris-use missal has a checked original colophon and bounded Maundy Thursday folios. Neither a first composition date for those prayers nor a predecessor relationship follows.

evidence.locus: Original scan PDF pp. 155–156, fol. lxix recto–verso, and p. 494 colophon; Usuarium book 79 contents pp. 152–180
evidence.claim: Original folios identify bounded Maundy Thursday prayer/rubric material; the colophon dates the Dupré and Huym printing to 22 September 1481.

stages.limitations: The scan and selected leaves do not certify full physical or textual completeness; 1685, 1705 and 1738 originals are uncollated.
stages.reception: The local-use designation identifies the intended book tradition; actual adoption by every church and any continuing-use interval have not been established.

stages.label: 1495 Rouen Missale Rothomagense
stages.scope: Identified book witness and the Eucharistic components supported by the cited original leaves or edition-identified contents index; no complete reconstructed missal.
stages.summary: Martin Morin’s identified Rouen print supplies a dated book witness with a contents map; later 1604, 1690 and 1728 entries remain bibliographic successors only.

evidence.locus: Book 81 identity lines 11–21; contents pp. 7, 9, 23, 148–195 and 289–437
evidence.claim: The catalogue identifies a Rouen-use printed missal and indexes temporal and sanctoral Masses, Ordinary, prefaces, Canon and local ceremony entries.

stages.limitations: Catalogue page headings are not inspected prayer bodies or proof of a distinct revision or diocesan adoption.
stages.reception: The local-use designation identifies the intended book tradition; actual adoption by every church and any continuing-use interval have not been established.

stages.label: 1520 Langres Missale Lingonense
stages.scope: Identified book witness and the Eucharistic components supported by the cited original leaves or edition-identified contents index; no complete reconstructed missal.
stages.summary: The 1520 Troyes printing identifies a Langres-use Mass book and advertises additions, but the title does not by itself prove exactly which texts changed against the circa 1492 witness.

evidence.locus: Book 318 original-title lines 11–21; contents pp. 7, 9, 21–37, 185–237, 357–363 and 618
evidence.claim: The transcribed title advertises additional recent feasts and sequences; the contents locate general rubrics, Ordinary, Canon, Mass cycles and colophon.

stages.limitations: The older circa 1492 preparation excerpt edited by Legg is not a checked whole missal here; no direct comparison or borrowing direction is established.
stages.reception: The local-use designation identifies the intended book tradition; actual adoption by every church and any continuing-use interval have not been established.

evidence.locus: Book 663 title and identity lines 11–23; contents pp. 1, 15, 127–165, 273–470
evidence.claim: The catalogue identifies the Uzès-use 1495 print, with calendar, Mass cycles, prefaces, Canon, sequentional and an appended priestly Mass order.

stages.limitations: Usuarium lists BL IB.41819 while the earlier Legg-based inventory cites IB.41877 for the extracted Ordo; copy identity must be reconciled before treating the records as one physical witness.
stages.reception: The local-use designation identifies the intended book tradition; actual adoption by every church and any continuing-use interval have not been established.

stages.label: Undated Sens Missale Senonense, circa 1527

stages.summary: BnF identifies an undated Sens missal edition whose title advertises a Dedication preface; this establishes an edition claim, not its first textual appearance.

evidence.locus: BP16_105469, Full title, Address, Edition date, Notes and Localizations
evidence.claim: The title advertises a Dedication preface after the Canon as never printed before; BnF dates this undated edition approximately from publishers and mark.

stages.limitations: The sole listed Durham copy is incomplete at the end; the preface, its placement and earlier Sens editions have not been collated. The approximate year is not an exact chronology point.
stages.reception: The local-use designation identifies the intended book tradition; actual adoption by every church and any continuing-use interval have not been established.

stages.label: 1738 Missale Parisiense, BnF B-178
stages.scope: Identified Paris-use missal edition and scholarly described Maundy Thursday postcommunion 1060; no original 1738 prayer body or whole-book text has been checked.
stages.witness_label: Missale Parisiense, 1738, BnF B-178; Usuarium book 7371
stages.summary: The exact BnF holding and year are catalogued. Ward discusses postcommunion 1060 in the 1738 Paris missal, while O’Connor’s MP annotation points to earlier Paris missals; neither establishes first introduction in 1738.

evidence.locus: Usuarium book 7371, identity fields: title, origin, age, shelfmark and Amiet 747
evidence.claim: Identifies a 1738 Paris missal edition and BnF B-178 holding.
Identifies the Maundy Thursday postcommunion as no. 1060 in the edited 1738 Paris missal.

evidence.locus: Annotated orations, entry 1060 and abbreviation MP
evidence.claim: The aggregate MP source mark points to Paris missals of 1685 and 1705, leaving the first introduction unresolved.

stages.limitations: The original Gallica scan linked from Usuarium returned 403 in the earlier inventory research; the 1738 original and 1685/1705 comparators are uncollated. No prayer wording is transcribed here, no 1481-to-1738 revision is asserted, and the catalogue year is not an effective-use date.
stages.reception: Publication and later scholarly identification do not establish adoption in every Paris church, a first-use date or continued observance.

stages.label: 1728 Missale ecclesiae Rotomagensis, BM Lyon 20390
stages.scope: Bibliographically identified Rouen missal witness only; the component designation reflects its missal genre and no original prayer or rubric has been inspected.
stages.witness_label: Missale ecclesiae Rotomagensis, 1728, BM Lyon 20390; Usuarium book 7090
stages.summary: Usuarium identifies a 1728 Rouen missal at BM Lyon 20390 under Amiet 1364. A second Usuarium row, 7461, has the same title, year and Amiet number; this does not establish a second edition or independent textual state.

evidence.locus: Usuarium book 7090, identity fields: original title, origin, age, BM Lyon 20390 and Amiet 1364; Amiet catalogue row 1364 for books 7090 and 7461
evidence.claim: Identifies the 1728 Rouen missal witness and exposes a possible duplicate catalogue row.

stages.limitations: No original 1728 book pages or paired 1495 text have been inspected. The book cannot establish a substantive reform, direct ancestry, text inheritance or actual diocesan uptake. Usuarium 7090 and 7461 may be duplicate descriptions; the physical relationship remains unresolved.
stages.reception: The Rouen designation is bibliographic; local approval, first use and parish reception have not been demonstrated.
